blocks.text: Aa'isha! Jibra'eel (AS) is here and he conveys Salaams to you." Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied by saying, "وَعَلَيْكَ السَّلَامُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللّٰهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهٗ". She was about to add to these words when Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The Salaam ends at that." Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) then said, "May the mercy and blessings of Allaah be on you, O Ahlul Bayt (members of Rasulullaah ﷺ's household)."[^1]
The Incident of Rasulullaah ﷺ with Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA)

Hadhrat Anas (RA) and other Sahabah (RA) narrate that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once requested permission to enter the home of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted with the words: "اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللّٰهِ". Although Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) replied by saying, "وَعَلَيْكَ السَّلَامُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللّٰهِ", he did so in a voice that was not audible to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted three times and each time, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) replied in a voice that was inaudible to Rasulullaah ﷺ. When Rasulullaah ﷺ turned to leave (thinking that no one was at home), Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) ran after him saying, "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Every greeting of yours fell on my ears and I had replied each time in a voice that you could not hear. I did that because I wanted to get more of your Salaams and blessings (because Salaam is a du'aa for peace and blessings)." He then took Rasulullaah ﷺ into his house and served some olive oil, which Rasulullaah ﷺ ate. After eating, Rasulullaah ﷺ made the du'aa:

blocks.arabic_text: أَكَلَ طَعَامَكُمُ الْأَبْرَارُ وَصَلَّتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَلَآئِكَةُ وَأَفْطَرَ عِنْدَكُمُ الصَّائِمُوْنَ
blocks.text: "May the pious eat your food, may the angels pray for you and may fasting people end their fasts with you."[^2]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to visit the Ansaar and when he came to the locality of the Ansaar, the children of the Ansaar would gather around him. He would then make du'aa for them, pass his hand over their heads and greet them with Salaam. When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived at the door of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA)'s house, he greeted with the words: "اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللّٰهِ". Although Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) replied, he did so in a voice that was not audible to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted three times and it was his practice never to greet more than three times (when seeking permission to enter). He would usually enter when granted permission or leave (if no one replied after three Salaams). Rasulullaah ﷺ therefore turned to leave (thinking that no one was at home), when Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) came running after him. The rest of the narration is the same as the one above.[^3]
